title: The popular version. Two brothers flipped a coin, and the winner made history.
description:
Two brothers flipped a coin, and the winner made history. The coin toss is real. It just did not hand the first flight to the man who won it.

Wilbur won the toss. His attempt failed. He put it down to a trifling error from inexperience with the machine and its starting method.

The Flyer needed three days of repairs. NASA Glenn dates the next attempt to 17 December.

Orville made the first flight. It began at 10:35 in the morning, into a very strong headwind. Over the ground it managed about 7 to 8 mph.

The length of the first flight on 17 December 1903. It covered 120 feet.

Wilbur flew the furthest, 852 feet. That flight lasted nearly a minute. Each brother flew twice, four flights in all.

The winner of the coin toss was not the first to fly.

Sources:
- https://www.history.com/news/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-the-wright-brothers (read): the brothers flipped a coin on 14 December 1903 to decide who would test the Flyer first; Wilbur won, his attempt failed and caused minor damage; on 17 December Orville piloted the first flight, airborne for 12 seconds and 120 feet; Wilbur's final flight that day covered 852 feet in nearly a minute.
- https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/K-12/email.htm (read): NASA Glenn page: coin flipped for the first attempt on 14 December, Wilbur won and crashed on takeoff, repairs took three days, next attempt 17 December; each brother made two flights, four in total; first flight 120 feet in 12 seconds, about 7 to 8 mph over the ground, into a very strong headwind; longest flight 59 seconds and 852 feet.
- https://blogs.libraries.wright.edu/news/outofthebox/2017/12/17/december-17-1903-success-four-flights/ (read): Wright State University Libraries: Wilbur won the toss and piloted the unsuccessful first try from Big Kill Devil Hill, blaming a trifling error from inexperience with the machine and its starting method; Orville flew 120 feet in 12 seconds at 10:35 a.m.; Wilbur flew 852 feet in 59 seconds.
